**Finding: deviation (critical) — Section 13, ¶p0088**

Section 13 vests in Garman "all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto)" and states that no title passes to Sparkling. Because "Modifications" are the bespoke changes in Schedule "D" that Sparkling commissions and pays for, Garman would own work product we fund, with only the narrow non-transferable use licence in Section 2 coming back to us. Separately, the Agreement is silent on ownership of Sparkling's data, despite Section 4(b) requiring Garman to convert it.

Redline (validated, preferred level):
- Narrows Garman's ownership to the Work "as it exists independently of this Agreement" (its platform ownership is unobjectionable) and makes the no-title sentence subject to the Agreement's express grants.
- Adds a new paragraph: Sparkling owns the Modifications and other work product developed specifically for and paid for by it (Garman assigns), with a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence back to any embedded Garman background IP; Sparkling retains all rights in its data, including data converted under Section 4; no joint ownership.
- Fallback offered in the comment: Garman may keep title to modifications of its own code if we receive a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense them.
